Adventure barter Show-artifact reply: native source reconstruction

This is binary source material. No game process, window, translator, generated
test input, translation assertion or acceptance check is used. The Python source
extractor reads the two configured Windows images with the fixed native objdump.

Complete producer boundaries (PE unwind, end exclusive):
  Steam:   0x14065a250 .. 0x14065bfaa
  Classic: 0x140657c70 .. 0x1406599ca
  Earlier ELF Ghidra C: announcement-conversation/elf-artifact-rumor.c,
                       native_supplier_0x10108c0.

The complete current PE bodies, every decoded conditional edge, compare, call,
literal load and supplier switch are retained in this directory. The normalized
source below omits string allocation and container lookup mechanics; it retains
every visible production and native silent alternative. Unresolved game-record
fields use the native offset/predicate rather than a guessed enum name.

Actual Show caller and downstream text ownership

Steam input 0x273c74..0x273c8c supplies:
  rcx = complete_reply_body string, initially empty
  edx = selected artifact record's id
  r8  = barter_screen+0x08, merchant/speaker unit
  r9  = barter_screen+0x10, recipient unit
  fifth argument = 0 (no conversation reference accumulator)
The paired Classic call is 0x27184c.

The first selected artifact builds whole_speaker_caption + ": "; later selected
artifacts append the native empty separator. Each body is merged at 0x273c9c,
then 0x273cb3 calls 0x8e7310 with width 0x44 and stores the resulting line array
at barter_screen+0x340. Renderer 0x270060..0x27009b reads that array and draws
each already wrapped line with 0xad9960; its draw return is 0x2700a0. This is the
same complete message visible in the screenshot. Translating an individual
wrapped draw line cannot recover every complete production and typed field.

The complete downstream ownership functions are extracted here as well:
  Steam string -> vector wrapper: 0x8e7310 .. 0x8e7431
  Steam vector -> wrapped rows:   0x8e7440 .. 0x8e7716
  Steam reply string drawing:    0xad9960 .. 0xad9a33
  Classic counterparts:          0x8e4b80 .. 0x8e4ca1,
                                 0x8e4cb0 .. 0x8e4f86,
                                 0xad69a0 .. 0xad6a73
All boundaries are RVAs with exclusive ends. The string wrapper copies the
complete input into one owned string pointer, calls the vector wrapper with
the original output vector and width, then destroys only its temporary input.
The output vector retains the allocated wrapped strings used by the renderer.
That retained ownership permits recovery after an earlier pre-wrap call is no
longer available: the original reply array, row-string addresses and contents
establish one complete report, independently of how its words happen to look.

The vector wrapper wraps only after the accumulated byte length exceeds width
(Steam 0x8e74ff..0x8e750a). It backtracks in the input to ASCII space 0x20 or
the start (0x8e7530..0x8e7550). A normal break at source index k retains that
space at the end of the emitted row: if the overflowing byte is at index i,
the backtracked count is i-k, so new_length = old_length-(i-k), including k
(0x8e7578..0x8e7599). The next pass advances beyond k and skips additional
ASCII spaces while the new-row flag is set (0x8e7617, 0x8e7636 and
0x8e74c6..0x8e74e2). Concatenating the retained raw rows therefore preserves
the ordinary word separator without inserting another space. Repeated spaces
after a break can be discarded by the native wrapper; their original count
cannot be recovered from the retained rows. The native special branch where
the backtracked count equals the entire accumulated length instead inserts
one ASCII space into the source at saved_index-1 (0x8e7552..0x8e7573).
It does not establish a generic whitespace or punctuation break rule.

The drawing wrapper has a materially different ABI from a function that reads
all four integer argument registers. At entry, 0xad9977 saves R9d as an optional
length limit, 0xad997a saves RCX as the drawing owner and RDX supplies the native
string. No instruction consumes the incoming R8. The wrapper later writes
R8b=1 itself at 0xad99f6 for the individual-byte drawing call. Consequently a
capture bridge must preserve the unused incoming R8 slot and forward the
fourth argument in R9; treating the wrapper as a three-argument function would
move the length limit into the unused slot. An uncaptured or retained draw is
still the complete native row, not a new sentence or standalone name field.

The caller has no nonempty-body guard between 0x273c8c and 0x273cb3. The
speaker header is already present when the producer's missing speaker/HF/
artifact paths return without a body (0x65a2ab/0x65a2d6/0x65a31a/0x65a368 to
0x65bf78). A first reply can therefore contain only SPEAKER + ": "; later
empty replies add no visible text. This is a static native branch, not an
observed game occurrence. The same wrapper retains the original typed speaker
after the caller capitalizes it at 0x273c3c.

Normalized producer

artifact_reply(out, artifact_id, speaker_unit, recipient_unit, refs) {
  if (!speaker_unit) return;
  speaker = lookup_speaker_historical_figure(speaker_unit);
  if (!speaker) return;
  artifact = lookup_artifact(artifact_id);
  if (!artifact) return;

  // Initialize from artifact+0x108..0x120, then merge the speaker's current
  // knowledge/memory tables and affiliation/identity caches. Site/building/HF/
  // region/underground ids are typed and are not inferred from name spelling.
  location = known_artifact_location(artifact, speaker_unit, speaker);
  firsthand = location.native_source_pointer != null; // rsp+0x70

  if (speaker.personal_claim(artifact_id).status_at_0x10 == -1) {
    out += "I desire that " + OBJECT(artifact) + " be returned to me.";
  }
  if (out.empty() && speaker.family_claim(artifact_id).status_at_0x10 == -1) {
    out += "I desire that " + OBJECT(artifact) + " be returned to my family.";
  }

  if (out.empty()) {
    for (link : speaker.entity_links) {
      if (link.virtual_type() != 10 && link.virtual_type() != 13) continue;
      entity = resolve_entity(link.id);
      if (!entity) continue;
      if (entity.type == 5) {
        // Native item material virtual+0x38 must return 0, virtual+0x40 must
        // index a valid inorganic; inorganic+0x40 >= 3 and its flag byte
        // (+0x38 pointee)+2 contains bit 0x20.
        if (primordial_material_native_predicate(artifact.item)) {
          out += ENTITY(entity.id)
            + " believes that primordial remnants such as " + OBJECT(artifact)
            + " belong back in their rightful home.";
          destination = resolve_entity_destination(entity);
          if (destination.site) {
            out += "  Any should be brought to " + DESTINATION(destination)
              + ", or given to one of us.";
          }
        }
      } else if (entity.artifact_claim(artifact_id).status_at_0x14 == -1) {
        out += "Speaking as a representative of " + ENTITY(entity.id)
          + ", it is important that " + OBJECT(artifact) + " be returned.";
        assignment = resolve_position_assignment(entity, claim);
        if (!assignment) {
          out += "  It is a valuable treasure to us.";
        } else if (position = resolve_position(entity, assignment)) {
          position_name = gender_selected_position_name(position, speaker.sex);
          if (assignment.hf_id == speaker.hf_id) {
            out += "  I require it as a symbol of the " + position_name + ".";
          } else if (assignment.hf_id != -1) {
            out += "  " + HF(assignment.hf_id, speaker_context)
              + " requires it to be a proper " + position_name + ".";
          } else {
            out += "  It is the symbol of the " + position_name + ".";
          }
        } // assignment exists but position does not: no reason sentence
        destination = resolve_entity_destination(entity);
        if (destination.site)
          out += "  It should be brought to " + DESTINATION(destination) + ".";
      }
      if (!out.empty()) break;
    }
  }

  if (out.empty() && (home = resolve_collection_home(speaker))
      && (artifact.item.virtual_tool_use(0x14) || artifact.item.type() == 0x59)) {
    // This branch reverses the ordinary artifact/item order.
    out += "It would be wonderful if " + REVERSED_OBJECT(artifact)
      + " found a lasting home within "
      + BUILDING(home.site_id, home.building_id, use_name=true, flags=0) + ".";
  }

  if (out.empty() && speaker_current_site_matches_subject_site()) {
    for (request : subject_site.artifact_requests) {
      if (request.flags & 1) continue;
      if (request.type != 0 || request.artifact_id != artifact_id) continue;
      out += REQUESTER(request) + " wants " + OBJECT(artifact);
      if (request.site_id != -1) out += " returned";
      out += "."; // this local branch intentionally does not append a site
      if (!out.empty()) break;
    }
  }

  if (out.empty()) {
    // The native related-entity/site search and request predicates are all in
    // the full instruction body: 0x65b399..0x65b899. Related site sets contain
    // the native 0x25 and 0x01 flag alternatives and site-type 0/1 restrictions.
    for (site : native_related_request_sites(speaker)) {
      for (request : site.artifact_requests) {
        if (request.flags & 1) continue;
        if (request.type != 0 || request.artifact_id != artifact_id) continue;
        out += REQUESTER(request) + " wants " + OBJECT(artifact);
        if (request.site_id != -1)
          out += " returned to " + DESTINATION(request);
        out += ".";
        if (!out.empty()) break;
      }
      if (!out.empty()) break;
    }
  }

  if (out.empty()) out += OBJECT(artifact) + "...";
  out += "  ";

  if (!speaker_has_active_impersonation() && location.hf_id == speaker.hf_id) {
    out += firsthand ? "Last I remember, I had it." : "Last I heard, I had it.";
    location_record_type = 0x1c;
  } else if (recipient_hf_resolves() && location.hf_id == recipient_hf.id) {
    if (!firsthand) out += "Last I heard, you held it.";
    // Firsthand recipient possession produces no location text.
  } else if (location.hf_id != -1) {
    out += firsthand ? "Last I saw, it was held by " : "Last I heard, it was held by ";
    out += HF(location.hf_id, speaker_context, native_flag=true) + ".";
    location_record_type = 0x1c;
  } else if (location.site_id != -1) {
    out += firsthand ? "Last I saw, it was in " : "Last I heard, it was in ";
    out += DESTINATION(location) + ".";
    location_record_type = 0x19;
  } else if (location.region_id != -1) {
    out += firsthand ? "Last I saw, it was in " : "Last I heard, it was in ";
    out += REGION(location.region_id, flags=0) + ".";
    location_record_type = 0x1a;
  } else if (location.underground_id != -1) {
    out += firsthand ? "Last I saw, it was in " : "Last I heard, it was in ";
    out += UNDERGROUND(location.underground_id, flags=0) + ".";
    location_record_type = 0x1b;
  } else {
    out += "I have no idea where it is.";
  }

  // Retain native location memory and conversation routing. These side effects
  // generate no additional visible strings. refs is null in the barter caller.
  if (recipient_is_player && recipient != speaker && valid_location_record)
    retain_native_location_memory(location_record_type, artifact, location);
  capitalize_native_initial(out);
}

Typed field suppliers and empty-output alternatives

OBJECT(a) = ARTIFACT(a.id) + OPTIONAL_DESCRIPTION(a).
REVERSED_OBJECT(a) = OPTIONAL_DESCRIPTION_BEFORE(a) + ARTIFACT(a.id).
Description is included when artifact+0x7a != 0, or item type == 0x59, or virtual
item tool-use(0x14) is true, or item type == 0x57. The item caption call is
Steam 0xc65450 / Classic 0xc62490 with native r8=1,r9=1. Ordinary ordering adds
a literal single space before the physical item description; reversed ordering
adds it after the physical item description. The item function is a complete
chained unwind owner and both regions are retained.

ARTIFACT: 0xb94400 / 0xb91440. Existing name is whole language_name. An empty
name uses Untitled for the native book/tool/0x57 alternatives; otherwise it uses
the physical item caption (native r8=0,r9=1). Invalid artifact => an unknown
artifact. Item caption production can contribute an empty string. Every caller
in this producer uses flags=0, so optional LPAGE tags never appear here.

ENTITY: 0xb92900 / 0xb8f940. Valid entity => whole entity.name, which may be
empty; missing entity => an unknown civilization. flags=0 here.

HF: 0xb92f10 / 0xb8ff50. Whole typed historical-person description, relative to
the speaker's HF, supports proper name, known identity, Nameless, unidentified
creature, race/caste description, a/the, zombie/ghostly modifiers and the native
self forms. Missing HF => an unknown creature. The emitted proper-name field
can be empty. The full context-dependent body remains in both native sources.

REQUESTER(q): if q.hf_id != -1, emit HF(q.hf_id), then " of " only when entity
id != -1; if entity id != -1, emit ENTITY(q.entity_id). If both ids are -1 the
requester is empty. The main producer still emits " wants " and the object.

DESTINATION(d): if d.building_id != -1, emit BUILDING(d.site_id,d.building_id,
use_name=true,flags=0) + " in "; always emit SITE(d.site_id,flags=0). In entity
destination branches building inclusion depends on a non-null building record,
equivalent to the id predicate after lookup. Empty named site/building outputs
do not suppress the literal " in " or final period.

BUILDING: 0xb94090 / 0xb910d0. Valid named building + native use-name predicate
=> whole language_name. Missing site/building or unknown top-level type => an
unknown building. Otherwise the 0..13 type switch yields a counting house,
a hospital, a guildhall, a mead hall, a keep, a temple, a library, a tavern,
a dark tower, an underworld spire, a market, a tomb, a tower, or the nested
type-6 underground-building subtype. Nested subtype 0 => a dungeon, 1 => the
sewers, 2 => the catacombs; any other nested subtype contributes no text.
The native switch table retains the exact type-to-branch mapping.

SITE: 0xb93930 / 0xb90970. Valid record => whole language_name, which may be
empty; absent record => an unknown site.
REGION: 0xb94a40 / 0xb91a80. Valid record => whole language_name, which may be
empty; absent record => an unknown region.
UNDERGROUND: 0xb94940 / 0xb91980. Valid record whose byte+0x7a is zero gives
type 0 => the depths of the world, type 1 => the magma sea, type 2 => the
Underworld. A nonzero byte+0x7a or any other type contributes no text. Missing
record => an unknown underground region. No generated regional name is read on
this path.

POSITION: the producer reads position base name at +0x98, female name +0xd8
when sex=0 and that variant has length>0, male name +0x118 when sex=1 and that
variant has length>0; all other cases use base name. A resolved position with
an empty name is not suppressed: its surrounding sentence and period remain.

Previously absent visible productions

The pre-existing adventure-announcement grammar had the principal request and
location sentences, but omitted the native no-destination "{holder} wants
{object}." and final "{object}..." fallback. Its lasting-home field was typed
as a generic name although the actual call is the complete building supplier.
Present-but-empty name/position/building fields also retain their surrounding
literal text; source productions must not assume every typed field is nonempty.
